subject: maths
question: 8 men and 12 women can build a wall in 10 days. 6 men and 8 women can build the same wall in 14 days. How many more days will 1 woman take to build that wall alone compared to the number of days 1 man will take to build the wall?
solution:
**Given:**

8 men and 12 women can build a wall in 10 days.

6 men and 8 women can build the same wall in 14 days.

**Formula used:**

Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Let the efficiency of a man be 'm' and of a woman be 'w'.

The total work done is the same in both cases. Therefore:

⇒ (8m + 12w) × 10 = (6m + 8w) × 14

⇒ 80m + 120w = 84m + 112w

⇒ 120w - 112w = 84m - 80m

⇒ 8w = 4m

⇒ 1m = 2w

**Find the number of days for 1 man and 1 woman to build the wall:**

From the first case: Total work = (8m + 12w) × 10

⇒ Total work = (8 × 2w + 12w) × 10 = 28w × 10 = 280w

Efficiency of 1 man = 2w, so time taken by 1 man = ​(280w)/(2w) = 140 days

Efficiency of 1 woman = w, so time taken by 1 woman = (280w)/(w) = 280 days

Difference in days = (280 - 140 = 140) days.

**∴ 1 woman will take 140 more days than 1 man to build the wall.**
